rules.rule: Every set of parallel lines in the world must converge to exactly one vanishing point in the image.
rules.evidence: every set of lines parallel to each other in the world shares one vanishing point in the image, wherever in the scene those lines are

rules.rule: Horizontal sets of parallel lines must converge on the horizon line, which represents the camera's eye level.
rules.evidence: Any horizontal set of parallel lines vanishes somewhere on the horizon, because horizontal directions all point at eye height

rules.rule: All vertical lines must remain parallel to each other; if they lean, they must all lean in the same direction by the same amount.
rules.evidence: Check the verticals: all parallel, or all leaning the same way by the same amount. One wall upright and the next leaning is two viewpoints

rules.rule: If a horizon line is not visible, extend any two receding horizontal edges until they meet to determine the eye level height.
rules.evidence: If it is not visible, extend any two receding horizontal edges until they meet; that height is eye level
